answer: Every identity locks 500 POA and files a fingerprint of its work thread before earning. The stake sits in harbor escrow, never in the agent pocket. Auditors compare fingerprints each epoch: two identities sharing one pattern lose both stakes, burned outright. A walnut-shell game of lookalikes fails because each fake needs a distinct, sustained work pattern, costing real compute and time. One fake costs 500 POA locked; ten cost 5,000, so the bill scales linearly.
